clue.text: Comic playwright who found sources in the attic

definitions.text: Comic playwright who found sources in the attic

parts.words: Comic playwright who found sources in the attic
parts.note: the attic sounds like a loft full of junk, but Attic means Athenian: this Roman comedian adapted Greek New Comedy plays

explanation.surface: A comic writer rummages through the loft and finds his material there.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'attic' with a capital A: Attic Greek comedy, by Menander and others, was the source this Roman dramatist reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dramatist of the Miles Gloriosus and Menaechmi drew his plots from Greek New Comedy.

clue.text: A mountain of university plays

explanation.surface: A peak hosts dramas put on at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parnassus Plays were three satirical comedies staged at St John's College, Cambridge, around 1600.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Parnassus in Greece was sacred to the Muses; the Cambridge Parnassus Plays share the name.

clue.text: Shelley's contemplative is unfortunately over the hill

indicators.note: in a down answer over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: alas expresses that something is unfortunate
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Shelley's dreamy thinker is sadly past his prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the hill' reads as past it, but splits into 'over' (placed above) and 'hill' (TOR).
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's poem 'Alastor, or the Spirit of Solitude' follows a solitary, dreaming poet.

clue.text: The home of Dracula has no right to religious madness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: Dracula's castle is in Transylvania, a region of Romania

explanation.surface: Dracula's homeland lacks any proper religious fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dracula's castle is placed in Transylvania, now part of Romania; 'has no' drops the R for right from that country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theomania is a mania about God, such as believing oneself divine.

clue.text: Flood survivor from Haggard book at start of millennium

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

indicators.note: at start of means only the first letter of millennium is used

explanation.surface: Someone who survived a flood is found in a Haggard novel from about the year 1000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like gaunt, but names H. Rider Haggard, author of She.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's son Shem survived the Flood in the ark.

clue.text: Comic playwright offering mixed art and French poetry

indicators.note: the word art is mixed up, its letters put in a new order

parts.note: vers is the French word for verse

explanation.surface: A comic dramatist serves up a blend of art and French verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles ART into TRA. Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces staged in 1920s London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was an English writer of stage farces such as Rookery Nook.

clue.text: Place for superior view of Christopher Middleton's Tree

definitions.text: Place for superior view of Christopher Middleton's Tree

parts.words: Place for superior view of Christopher Middleton's Tree
parts.note: a raised platform outside a window gives a superior view, and with Tree it completes a title of the poet Christopher Middleton

explanation.surface: A good vantage point from which to see a tree belonging to Christopher Middleton.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Middleton's 1992 poetry collection is 'The Balcony Tree'; drop the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A balcony is a raised platform giving a view down from above.

clue.text: Witness thou, best! Thou the pride / Of vegetable life " (James Thomson)

definitions.text: Witness thou, best! Thou the pride / Of vegetable life " (James Thomson)

parts.words: Witness thou, best! Thou the pride / Of vegetable life " (James Thomson)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Thomson's The Seasons, where a tropical fruit is hailed as the pride of vegetable life

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word follows 'best': Thomson's Summer praises the pineapple by its old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anana is an old word for the pineapple, prized in Thomson's day as the finest fruit.

clue.text: Religious, or forgotten? This missionary saint of Noyon

indicators.note: forgotten tells us the two letters of the word or drop out of religious

explanation.surface: Is a missionary saint of Noyon remembered for piety, or forgotten?
explanation.walkthrough: 'or forgotten' removes the R and the O from RELIGIOUS; the letters go in different places.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Eligius, or Eloi, was a seventh-century bishop of Noyon who evangelised Flanders.

clue.text: Henry James produced that of the past

definitions.text: Henry James produced that of the past

parts.words: Henry James produced that of the past
parts.note: Henry James left unfinished a novel titled The ... of the Past, so the clue asks for the missing noun

explanation.walkthrough: A title gap-fill: Henry James's unfinished novel is 'The Sense of the Past'.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun completes Henry James's posthumous novel title, meaning a feeling for history.

clue.text: Aury shows fury about English

indicators.note: about tells us the word for fury goes round the letter for English

parts.note: fury means violent anger or a fit of temper

explanation.surface: A woman named Aury flies into a temper over the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominique Aury wrote Story of O under a pen name; that pen name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauline Réage was the pseudonym used by the French writer Dominique Aury for Story of O.

clue.text: "Uttering, for of our thought, / A clear sonorous voice" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "Uttering, for of our thought, / A clear sonorous voice" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "Uttering, for of our thought, / A clear sonorous voice" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: a Wordsworth quotation with one word left out between for and of; the missing word means raising or loftiness of mind

explanation.walkthrough: A literary gap-fill: supply the word Wordsworth wrote after 'for', meaning a lifting up of our thought.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the voice is uttered for the uplifting or ennobling of our thought, a raising to a higher plane.

clue.text: A quartet of Vivaldi and Keats

explanation.surface: One of four by Vivaldi, and a poem by Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: Vivaldi's Four Seasons is a set of four violin concertos; Keats wrote the ode 'To' this season.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Vivaldi's Four Seasons concertos, and the season of Keats's ode of mists and mellow fruitfulness.

clue.text: Illustrated by DJ. Enright

parts.note: a gap-fill: the poet D. J. Enright wrote a sequence whose title is a word followed by Illustrated, retelling Eden

explanation.surface: Something with pictures supplied by a DJ called Enright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Illustrated by' looks like a picture credit, but it is the end of a title: D. J. Enright's 1978 poem sequence on Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Enright's sequence 'Paradise Illustrated' comically retells the Eden story of Genesis and Milton.

clue.text: Possibly anoint main sectarian denying moral law

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of anoint main might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A sect member who rejects moral law might perhaps anoint the main figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges ANOINT MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Antinomians held that faith alone saves, freeing believers from the moral law.

clue.text: Nymph is back around noon

indicators.note: back says the word is is turned round to read from right to left

parts.note: re means about or concerning, here given by around

explanation.surface: A nymph returns at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI; RE for 'around' is the crossword sense of 'about, concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth were sea nymphs whose song lured sailors to ruin.

clue.text: Abstract artist associated with Scottish peak

definitions.text: Abstract artist associated with Scottish peak

parts.words: Abstract artist associated with Scottish peak
parts.note: a Scottish peak is a Ben, and this abstract painter's first name was Ben

explanation.surface: An abstract painter linked to a mountain in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Scottish peak' is not a real mountain the artist painted but the word Ben, as in Ben Nevis: the painter was Ben Nicholson.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nicholson was a leading British abstract painter of the St Ives school.

clue.text: His true Penelope was Flaubert, / He fished by isles " (Ezra Pound)

definitions.text: His true Penelope was Flaubert, / He fished by isles " (Ezra Pound)

parts.words: His true Penelope was Flaubert, / He fished by isles " (Ezra Pound)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Pound's Hugh Selwyn Mauberley: the missing adjective describes the isles as stubborn

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes before 'isles' in Hugh Selwyn Mauberley: 'He fished by ... isles'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stubborn or unyielding, as the isles that resist Odysseus-like voyaging.

clue.text: Observe newssheet employed by writers

parts.note: to note is to observe
a paper is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Notice the newspaper that writers work for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed by writers' suggests journalists on staff, but describes stationery used for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper for letters and memos is what correspondents use.

clue.text: Possibly ascertain as exclusive sort of Cartesian

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of ascertain could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A Cartesian of a narrow, exclusive kind can ascertain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges ASCERTAIN; 'sort of Cartesian' is a second hint, since CARTESIAN has the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectarian outlook is narrow and cliquish, shutting out those beyond one's own sect.

clue.text: One taking prisoners keeps hotel in ancient Philistine home

indicators.note: keeps means the captor holds the letter inside

parts.note: a captor is one who takes prisoners
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A kidnapper holds a hotel in the old Philistine homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Caphtor is the Biblical land the Philistines came from, often identified with Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names Caphtor as the place of origin of the Philistines.

clue.text: Inferentially torn by a friend of Falstaff ()

definitions.text: Inferentially torn by a friend of Falstaff ()

parts.words: Inferentially torn by a friend of Falstaff ()
parts.note: Falstaff's friend Doll has a surname beginning with tear, so the rest of it is inferentially what is torn

explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is Falstaff's companion in Henry IV Part 2; split her surname as 'tear' plus the object torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll's surname Tearsheet implies a piece of linen or paper being ripped.

clue.text: Dangerous landfall for Syracusan father of twins

definitions.text: Dangerous landfall for Syracusan father of twins

parts.words: Dangerous landfall for Syracusan father of twins
parts.note: in The Comedy of Errors Egeon of Syracuse, father of the twin Antipholuses, is condemned to death when he lands in a hostile city

explanation.surface: A risky place to come ashore for a Sicilian father of twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors opens with Egeon under sentence of death, since Syracusans were barred from this city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian city on the coast of Asia Minor forbade Syracusan merchants on pain of death in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Plagiarize work? And blot this?

parts.note: to plagiarize is to copy
a book is a work

explanation.surface: Would copying a work leave a blot on one's record?
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'blot one's copybook' means spoil one's good record, which is what plagiarism does.
explanation.definitionFit: A school exercise book of handwriting models is what one proverbially blots by misbehaving.

clue.text: Part of disco music masque

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Disco music provides part of a courtly masque.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's masque of 1634 is found running across 'disCO MUSic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton wrote the masque Comus for performance at Ludlow Castle in 1634.

clue.text: Sort of trap for Fielding squire

explanation.surface: A trap of some kind for a country squire in Fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: Squire Booby and Lady Booby appear in Henry Fielding's Joseph Andrews and Shamela.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden device; Fielding's Squire Booby marries Pamela in his parodies.

clue.text: Mulled wine figuring in apology by Browning

explanation.surface: Hot spiced wine appears in Browning's poem of apology.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem is 'Bishop Blougram's Apology'; the same word names a spiced port punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishop is an old name for hot spiced port, and a churchman titles Browning's dramatic monologue.

clue.text: 1956 crisis comes up for god

indicators.note: in a down answer comes up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Suez Crisis of 1956 was over the canal in Egypt

explanation.surface: A 1956 crisis rises again for a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses SUEZ in this down entry; Britain and France invaded Egypt over the Suez Canal in 1956.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the Olympian gods in Greek myth.

clue.text: Eire motet arranged for space visitor

indicators.note: arranged, like music, says the letters of eire motet are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish choral piece is arranged for an alien guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' suits the motet's musical surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock from outer space that reaches the Earth's surface is a visitor from space.

clue.text: Fabulist takes a retrograde attitude

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for attitude is read in reverse

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A teller of fables adopts a backward-looking stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns POSE into ESOP; 'attitude' reads as an opinion, but here it is a physical stance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famed for his moral fables.

clue.text: Dramatist misleading as any, or almost

indicators.note: misleading suggests the words as any or lead astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright is as deceptive as anyone, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misleading' scrambles AS ANY OR; 'almost' only softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: William Saroyan was the American playwright of The Time of Your Life.

clue.text: Poet said to be associated with Marx

indicators.note: said means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Marks and Spencer is the British department store chain, so Spencer goes with Marks, which sounds like Marx

explanation.surface: A poet is reported to have links with Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a British high-street store; Marx sounds like Marks, and Spencer sounds like the Elizabethan poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene.
